brief.title: Midterm brief: Tuesday, October 27
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Tuesday, October 27

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic; all 10 House forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats, from Inside Elections' 212 D / 205 R to 230 D at The Economist, FiftyPlusOne and Silver Bulletin ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 46 D and 44 R seats are solid or likely, with 10 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 91.5% for the House and 66.5% for the Senate, the Senate up two points ([Polymarket House](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026), [Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 27.

## What moved
- **Forecaster updates (Oct 26-27):** 17 rating changes, 11 toward Democrats and 6 toward Republicans ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). Split Ticket made 12 and reversed six seats back to its Oct 24 ratings; its column has flipped three days running, so treat it cautiously.
- **House consensus:** NJ-07 moved from Lean D to Likely D on Split Ticket's change, so it leaves the tracked list (61 races).
- **Senate:** Mississippi's consensus moved from Solid R to Likely R after RealClearPolling's change; Split Ticket moved South Carolina and Decision Desk HQ moved Nebraska from Likely R to Lean R ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). No poll average moved enough.

## Races to watch today
- **South Carolina Senate (Lean R):** Former South Carolina governors endorsed Democrat Annie Andrews over Graham ([The Guardian via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxNd3EtMUszUldVRUU5N2lsMVl5MW1Yeml6ZmFYUzBFNEZ6TmdQVGJPelNmdEwyWGlVRjZKVnZ0QzNrVGFhRWItQWhFbG94S2Z5cnpjbFpNcXY5VnJpT3RFb2tVV0IzM3R6QlI2VUk0LU0xMTRGREZ4NzJVbzFQWUQyOUVicEQyM0hIWHlZYzJ1REdBaFdEWWVXMA?oc=5)). Average: R+1.4.
- **Alaska Senate (Tossup):** A judge fast-tracked the Justice Department's lawsuit as Peltola seeks dismissal before Election Day ([CNBC via Google News](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Average: D+0.8.
- **Mississippi Senate (Likely R):** NPR asks whether Black turnout and Trump fatigue can break the state's red wall ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/27/nx-s1-6018592/mississippi-senate-trump-colom-black-voter-turnout)).
- **Kansas Senate (Tossup):** Vance returned to rally for Marshall ([KCTV via Google News](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Average: D+0.5.

## Early vote
These are ballots by party registration, not votes, and mail ballots have leaned Democratic since 2020.
- **North Carolina:** Through Oct 25, 1,583,181 ballots were cast, 136% of the 2022 total at the same point (1,163,784) ([NCSBE](https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Press/2026%20General/NC%20Absentee%20Stats%20for%202026%20General/2026-10-26%20Daily%20Absentee%20Stats%20Report%20-%202026%20General.pdf)). By Oct 26 the total reached 1,773,890 at D 41.0% / R 24.2%; the Democratic edge narrowed 1.2 points in a day ([NCSBE data file](https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=ENRS/2026_11_03/)).
- **Florida (Oct 26):** Registered Republicans now edge Democrats among 3,152,810 ballots, R 39.9% / D 39.5%, as in-person voting overtakes mail; registration is R 41.5% / D 30.1% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from Florida Division of Elections data).
- **Senate battlegrounds (Oct 26):** Arizona 956,224 at D 38.2% / R 38.7% (via a private compiler); Iowa 265,710 at D 50.6% / R 31.6%; Kansas 204,155 at D 46.9% / R 39.4%; Nebraska 151,915 at D 41.0% / R 42.2% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from secretary of state data).

## What the spectrum is saying
- **Left:** Pod Save America's new episode is titled "Let Them Eat Cheesecake"; the feed gives only the title ([Pod Save America](https://audioboom.com/posts/8969627)).
- **Center-left:** An NPR poll finds Democrats still poised for gains but with warning signs on how many ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/27/nx-s1-6017479/2026-midterms-npr-poll-democrats-trump-approval)).
- **Center-right:** The WSJ reports Talarico must convince some Texas voters he isn't too liberal ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/texas-senate-james-talarico-strategy-5024ef0d?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)).
- **Right:** National Review accuses El-Sayed's camp of anti-Catholicism ([National Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/10/anti-catholicism-lives-with-el-sayed-in-michigan/)). This is opinion, not reporting.

## Talking points
- Five generic ballot aggregators average D+8.7 as of Oct 25, from Decision Desk HQ's D+8.0 to FiftyPlusOne's D+9.2 ([Wikipedia aggregate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections#Generic_congressional_ballot_aggregate_polls)).
- The WSJ reports allies worry Thune could be blamed if Republicans lose the Senate ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/a-bruised-john-thune-leads-senate-gop-into-uncertain-future-1ab64435?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)).

## Coverage note
All 25 sources reported, including the new generic ballot table, and early vote covered 27 states. Kalshi had no priced markets. Candidate parties remain unresolved for seven House races (FL-22, NV-02, NY-21, NC-11, SC-01, TX-23, TX-35).
